fields.subnational_unit: Inkosi Langalibalele Local Municipality, KwaZulu-Natal (rural and low-income wards)
fields.population: community members and municipal councillors of Inkosi Langalibalele Local Municipality
fields.sample_size: 26 interview participants (community members and councillors, quotations coded Councillor 1-18 and Community Member 1-21), plus secondary data and SWOT analysis; no sampling or recruitment procedure described
fields.effect_measure: thematic analysis of interviews (three themes: state of service delivery; stakeholder engagement and participation; financial constraints and resource allocation) with a SWOT analysis; no quantitative measure
fields.effect_estimate: Persistent governance problems: unpredictable water supply and long distances to water points (municipal target: water within 200 m); maintenance backlogs of weeks to months; community members feel excluded from decisions and meetings are poorly publicised; budget constraints and funds earmarked for projects that do not meet residents' priorities; calls for transparency in financial management; PPPs seen as an opportunity with corruption risks. The authors argue corruption, mismanagement and misleading public communication matter more than funding alone (example: the Shayamoya Rural Housing Project completed 178 of 500 houses and the municipality's housing developer status was revoked). Recommends participatory budgeting, anti-corruption measures, staff training and PPPs under strict transparency. Literature statements: about 70% of households have piped water; 15% of supply systems non-functional (cited, not measured).
fields.model_type: qualitative thematic analysis with SWOT analysis
fields.study_design: qualitative case study with interviews (26 participants) and secondary data analysis

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative case study (26 interviews with community members and councillors) of water and sanitation delivery in Inkosi Langalibalele Local Municipality, KwaZulu-Natal, read in full text 2026-10-04. Governance failure, weak participation, budget misalignment and corruption risk; the methods section is missing so recruitment, data collection and analysis cannot be judged.
